name: IonQ
short_description: Trapped-ion quantum computers sold through cloud and direct access.
why_relevant: First pure-play quantum computing company to go public.
history: Founded in 2015 by physicists Chris Monroe and Jungsang Kim, IonQ spun out of pioneering trapped-ion research at the University of Maryland to build commercial quantum computers. It delivered cloud access via AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, and in 2021 became the first pure-play quantum company to list on the NYSE through a SPAC merger. Successive hardware generations (Harmony, Aria) improved qubit counts and fidelity, and IonQ later announced the Forte and Forte Enterprise systems for on-premises deployment. It now targets error-corrected logical qubits and utility-scale workloads across industry and national programs.

name: Rigetti Computing
short_description: Superconducting quantum processors in its own US foundry.
why_relevant: Surviving years of quantum scale to keep systems in the cloud.
history: Founded in 2013 by Chad Rigetti, Rigetti Computing built its own superconducting qubit foundry and introduced cloud-accessible quantum processors. In 2022 it went public on Nasdaq via a SPAC merger, and its Ankaa-generation chips steadily raised qubit counts and gate performance across the Aspen product line. The company built hybrid quantum-classical orchestration through its Quantum Cloud Services, partnering with major cloud and chip vendors. Today it continues developing superconducting systems and roadmap goals toward fault-tolerant computing while refining processors and software across commercial and government clients.

name: Quantinuum
short_description: Honeywell-minted quantum company with trapped-ion and logical-qubit advances.
why_relevant: Holds records for logical qubit error suppression in practice.
history: Formed in 2021 through the merger of Honeywell Quantum Solutions and Cambridge Quantum, Quantinuum combined trapped-ion hardware with advanced software and cybersecurity. Its H-series systems repeatedly set records, and its logical-qubit demonstrations with Microsoft suppressed errors far below physical qubit levels. The company raised a roughly $300M round in 2024 at a $7.7B valuation and expanded into quantum chemistry, QKD, and generative AI workloads. Today it operates H-series systems at scale and continues pursuing fault-tolerant milestones with US and European partners.

name: PsiQuantum
short_description: Photonics-based fault-tolerant quantum computer with billion-qubit roadmap.
why_relevant: The only fault-tolerant architecture that could scale in a fab.
history: Founded in 2016 by Jeremy O'Brien, Terry Rudolph, Mark Thompson, and Pete Shadbolt, PsiQuantum took a photonics-first approach to fault-tolerant quantum computing, betting that existing semiconductor manufacturing could scale single-photon qubits. It raised successive rounds backed by Bill Gates, BlackRock, and others, reaching a $6B+ valuation, and selected Brisbane, Australia, for its first utility-scale facility. The company builds cryogenic photonic control hardware with partners such as GlobalFoundries. PsiQuantum remains a private, fab-worthy contender aiming for a million-qubit, error-corrected quantum computer before rivals.

name: Xanadu
short_description: Photonic quantum computing with an open-source stack, PennyLane.
why_relevant: Bottleneck-free photonics model that avoids conflicting error correction.
history: Founded in 2016 in Toronto, Xanadu developed photonic quantum computers combined with machine learning and open-source software, most notably PennyLane. In 2022 it claimed quantum computational advantage with Borealis, a programmable photonic processor, following earlier X8 and X-Series systems. Xanadu built a vertically integrated stack spanning photonic chips, cloud deployment, and a large developer community. The company raised significant Canadian and international funding and today focuses on scaling hardware and demos in resource-efficient photonic architectures, targeting fault tolerance while keeping its software open.

name: QuEra
short_description: Neutral-atom quantum computers with all-to-all connectivity.
why_relevant: Aquila's 256-qubit machine is among the most accessible on AWS.
history: Founded in 2018 by researchers from Harvard and MIT, QuEra commercializes neutral-atom quantum computing with all-to-all connectivity. Its Aquila machine, a 256-qubit analog program, became broadly accessible on Amazon Braket, and the company launched a three-year roadmap to fault-tolerant machines including 10- and 30-logical-qubit systems. QuEra raised a $230M Series B in 2024 to close the gap to useful, error-corrected quantum computers. It pursues a hybrid of analog and digital operation, positioning its architecture as one of the most accessible on AWS and a leading path to scalable error correction.

name: PASQAL
short_description: European neutral-atom quantum computer with analog-hybrid time evolution.
why_relevant: EU's flagship neutral-atom hardware sold to European airlines and banks.
history: Founded in 2019 as a spin-out from France's Institut d'Optique, PASQAL builds neutral-atom quantum processors with analog-hybrid time evolution. It secured major European deployments, selling systems to banking and airline clients and supplying one of the first on-site quantum machines at a European national center. In 2024 PASQAL opened a US subsidiary in Boston and advanced its roadmap toward fault-tolerant machines, with a production facility in Massy, France. The company raised over $130M, positioning itself as the EU flagship for quantum hardware while expanding software partnerships and Quantum-as-a-Service offerings.

name: Atom Computing
short_description: Optical-tweezer arrays far past the 1,000-qubit mark.
why_relevant: First platforms announced past the 1,225-qubit frontier.
history: Founded in 2018, Atom Computing builds arrays of optically trapped neutral atoms and, in 2023, announced a 1,225-qubit system — then among the largest publicly disclosed — from its Berkeley, California base. Its nuclear-spin encoding reduces sensitivity to decoherence, and in 2024 it announced a co-designed product with Microsoft for logical-qubit demonstrations. The company partners with national labs and cloud providers to bring its systems online. Atom Computing remains privately held, focusing on scaling array sizes and error correction while commercializing full-stack hardware for early quantum utility.

name: D-Wave
short_description: Operates commercial quantum annealing systems for optimization.
why_relevant: Runs the only revenue-producing quantum systems sold to businesses.
history: Founded in 1999, D-Wave pioneered commercial quantum annealing, shipping its first system to Lockheed Martin in 2011 and subsequently installing machines at NASA, Volkswagen's research, and the University of Southern California. The company's Advantage processors raised qubit counts past 5,000 while real-world customers used quantum annealing for logistics and optimization. In 2022 D-Wave became a publicly listed company on the NYSE via SPAC. Now based in Burnaby, Canada, it is the only vendor reporting revenue-producing quantum systems, expanding into quantum hybrid and continuing its annealing-plus-gate roadmap.

name: IQM Quantum Computers
short_description: European leader in on-prem superconducting quantum computers.
why_relevant: Delivers full quantum computers to European national centers.
history: Founded in 2018 as a spin-out from Aalto University and VTT, IQM Quantum Computers builds full-stack on-premises superconducting systems and co-designed processors. It delivered complete quantum computers to European national institutions, including Finland, Germany (Leibniz), and France, and won landmark procurement in Germany's national roadmap projects. In 2023-24 IQM progressed toward a 54-qubit processor and a strategic production partnership with Soitec in Espoo, Finland. The company raised over €180M, positioning itself as the EU leader in local, sovereign quantum hardware with a strong consortium and education ecosystem.

name: Neuralink
short_description: Implantable brain-computer interface aiming to restore motor function.
why_relevant: Put hundreds of electrodes in human brains and streamed cursor control.
history: Founded in 2016 by Elon Musk and others, Neuralink developed ultra-thin thread electrodes and the surgical robot needed to place them. After private preclinical work and repeated fundraising, the company received FDA breakthrough-device designation in 2023 and began human trials in early 2024, streaming real-time cursor control from a patient's motor cortex. Participants have used the N1 implant to play video games and browse online; the Telepathy device emphasizes high channel count and long-term viability. Neuralink continues expanding multi-patient trials while upgrading hardware and eligibility criteria.

name: Synchron
short_description: Stentrode delivers brain signals via the blood vessels without open surgery.
why_relevant: Vascular route avoids craniotomy and broadens BCI eligibility.
history: Founded in 2016, Synchron developed the Stentrode, an endovascular brain-computer interface delivered through blood vessels, avoiding open-brain surgery. The company began small human feasibility studies in Australia and the US, receiving FDA Breakthrough Device designation in 2020. In late 2021 it became the first to obtain a US clinical trial for a permanently implanted BCI; the New York-based company later began the COMMAND trial, letting patients with severe paralysis message and click via a Bluetooth-connected Stentrode. Synchron continues expanding participants, strategic licensing, and pathways toward broader clinical availability.

name: Precision Neuroscience
short_description: Ultra-thin electrode arrays laid onto the brain's surface.
why_relevant: Micron-scale arrays with far less tissue damage than penetrating probes.
history: Founded in 2021 by former Neuralink and industry executives, Precision Neuroscience develops ultra-thin, micron-scale electrode arrays that sit on the brain's surface, minimizing tissue damage. The company received FDA approval for early human studies in 2023 and demonstrated the ability to read signals for potential cursor control. Its Layer 7 arrays pack thousands of electrodes and can be inserted through a small slit, positioning the firm for high-resolution, minimally invasive cortical interfaces. Headquartered in New York, Precision is scaling manufacturing and clinical partners in the emerging BCI ecosystem.

name: ONWARD Medical
short_description: Stimulates the spinal cord to restore movement after paralysis.
why_relevant: People with spinal injury can reach, grip and stand again via ARC therapy.
history: Founded in 2014, ONWARD Medical develops implantable and wearable spinal stimulation systems to restore movement after spinal cord injury. Building on decades of lab research, its ARC-EX external stimulator delivered clinically meaningful gains in hand and arm function in a pivotal North American trial, and the company filed for FDA clearance and CE certification of ARC-EX for arm recovery. In parallel, ARCIM transcutaneous and implantable programs target walking. The Eindhoven-based company is publicly traded on Euronext Brussels and is advancing therapy platforms toward broad regulatory approval and commercial launch.

name: Paradromics
short_description: High-data-rate neural implant for motor and sensory restoration.
why_relevant: Targets the highest channel counts in implanted BCI research.
history: Founded in 2015 as a research venture, Paradromics builds high-data-rate cortical implants for motor and sensory restoration. In 2021 it secured a multi-year DARPA contract to advance high-bandwidth human interface hardware, and it develops a cortical modem with thousands of electrode channels. The company's strategy emphasizes channel density and reliability for restoring speech, movement, and computerized voice. Based in Austin, Texas, Paradromics works toward its first human trials with a neuron-to-text pipeline and partnerships in neuroprosthetics.

name: Blackrock Neurotech
short_description: Silo-trusted implant leader with decades of human BCI deployments.
why_relevant: The hardware at the center of most landmark human BCI results.
history: Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Salt Lake City, Blackrock Neurotech is a longstanding implant leader, manufacturing the Utah array at the center of most landmark human BCI demonstrations. Its technology has enabled decades of research from cursor control to speech decoding and neuroprosthetic movement. Blackrock launched the first FDA-approved investigational BCI trial in 2023 and works with partners on advanced implant circuits and clinical systems. It continues to supply the research community while commercializing access for future patients, reinforcing its position as a critical infrastructure supplier for human neuroscience.

name: Magic Leap
short_description: Pioneered lightfield AR headsets, now focused on enterprise and defense.
why_relevant: Literally computer-generated light mixed with the real world.
history: Founded in 2010 by Rony Abovitz, Magic Leap raised billions to pioneer lightfield augmented-reality headsets, releasing the first Magic Leap 1 in 2018 after long secrecy. The company restructured, pivoting from a consumer focus toward enterprise, healthcare, and defense, and released Magic Leap 2 in 2022 with improved field of view and stability. After a series of layoffs and leadership transitions, it now develops lightfield optics for enterprise adoption and defense programs, headquartered in Plantation, Florida. Magic Leap remains a prominent spatial-computing firm despite its scaled-back ambitions.

name: Varjo
short_description: Human-eye-resolution XR headsets used by aviation and defense training.
why_relevant: Mixed-reality detail sharp enough to read cockpit instruments.
history: Founded in 2016 in Helsinki, Varjo developed bionic display XR headsets combining human-eye-resolution foveated displays with peripheral vision. Its hardware has become standard in aviation, defense, automotive, and medical training, with enterprise customers including major aerospace firms. Varjo released the XR-4 series in late 2023 and expanded into Software-in-the-Loop and telepresence products that stream photoreal scenes into headsets. The company remains a private European XR leader, operating in the enterprise segment with recurring revenue amid industry consolidation.

name: Lynx
short_description: Compact color see-through MR glasses using waveguide optics.
why_relevant: Framed-as glASses mixed worlds at a fraction of headset weight.
history: Founded in 2018 in Paris, Lynx develops compact color see-through mixed-reality glasses using waveguide optics and a design closer to standard eyewear than bulky headsets. After significant crowdfunding and pre-orders, the startup began shipping its Lynx-R1 headset, emphasizing lightweight, mobile MR for professional and consumer use. The company focuses on open architecture and the emerging AR glasses market. Despite supply-chain challenges common to the segment, Lynx continues pursuing its goal of affordable, glasses-form-factor mixed reality from its base in France.

name: Heart Aerospace
short_description: Hybrid-electric ES-30 recharging ground-era regional routes.
why_relevant: Noise-reduced ES-30 picked up by major airlines for 800 km hops.
history: Founded in 2018 in Sweden, Heart Aerospace developed the ES-30, a hybrid-electric regional aircraft targeting flights around 800 kilometers with dramatically lower noise. The company secured key airline partnerships, including United Airlines, Air Canada, and regional operators, to help shape its design and route planning. Heart raised significant venture funding and progressed its ES-30 platform and ground-recharging infrastructure, while also launching the ES-9 concept for battery-electric commuter flights. It continues working toward certification and commercial operations from its Gothenburg headquarters.

name: Beta Technologies
short_description: Builds the ALIA battery-powered aircraft and charging network.
why_relevant: Operates test flights across the Northeast charging corridor it built.
history: Founded in 2017 near Burlington, Vermont, Beta Technologies builds the ALIA aircraft family and a chartered network of electric-charging stations. The company flew early full-scale test aircraft, completed longer-range eVTOL test flights, and became an early US customer of the charging network with agreements across the Northeast. It raised over $1B, including a $375M round in 2023, and began working toward FAA certification of both the ALIA CTOL and VTOL variants. Beta combines aerospace engineering with on-the-ground energy infrastructure to enable regional electric flight.

name: Wisk Aero
short_description: Makes a fully autonomous two-seat eVTOL as a Boeing subsidiary.
why_relevant: Pioneers completely pilotless passenger flight certification.
history: Founded in 2010 as a Kitty Hawk-related venture and rebranded Wisk Aero, the company builds a fully autonomous, two-seat eVTOL air taxi with no onboard pilot. Acquired and restructured within Boeing's orbit in 2023, Wisk progressed its autonomous flight certification approach, operating between Kitty Hawk and New Zealand and partnering on vertiports. It remains a leader in pilotless passenger air taxi work, emphasizing safety and redundancy. Based in Mountain View, California, Wisk continues development toward commercial urban air mobility for future regulatory pathways.

name: PQShield
short_description: Hardens chips and systems against quantum-computer cryptanalysis.
why_relevant: Q-day migration in hardware before the AI wave outpaces signatures.
history: Founded in 2018 as an Oxford University spin-out, PQShield develops post-quantum cryptography IP, silicon, and integration tools to protect chips, documents, and systems against Q-day quantum cryptanalysis. It built close relationships with major hardware and security vendors and launched quantum-resistant implementations across TLS, chipsets, and US federal post-quantum standards. The company raised a $20M Series B in 2023 to accelerate production, hardening embedded devices for the post-quantum era. Headquartered in Oxford, UK, PQShield works with governments, semiconductor vendors, and industrial security to future-proof cryptography.

name: Shield AI
short_description: V-BAT AI pilots aircraft without GPS, comms or pilots.
why_relevant: Autonomy-anywhere pilots could redefine the pilot requirements of fleets.
history: Founded in 2015, Shield AI develops AI pilots enabling aircraft to operate without GPS, communications, or pilots. Its Hivemind autonomy runs edge AI for fixed-wing and VTOL aircraft, including the V-BAT drone, which has seen combat-compatible operations. The company raised over $1B, including a $200M round valuing it at $4B+. Shield AI now integrates its autonomy across defense platforms and strategic partners supporting customers globally, positioning itself as a leading autonomous-defense hardware-and-software provider.

name: Altos Labs
short_description: Invests in transient-youth-factor research to reverse cellular aging.
why_relevant: $3B bet that cellular rejuvenescence is a solvable biological problem.
history: Founded in 2021 with roughly $3B in backing, Altos Labs funds and runs research on cellular rejuvenation, including the transient expression of youth factors to reverse aging at the cellular level. It recruited prominent longevity scientists and established campuses in the San Francisco Bay Area, San Diego, Cambridge, and Japan, building one of the largest dedicated longevity teams. The company combines academic-style curiosity with deep capital, focusing on reprogramming, biomarkers, and therapeutic pathways toward extending healthspan. Headquartered in Redwood City, California, Altos continues scaling its scientific platform and partnerships.

name: Retro Biosciences
short_description: Runs aging-reversal programs in cells, mice and soon humans.
why_relevant: Atlas-platform bets decade-scale grants to defeat organismal aging.
history: Founded in 2021, Retro Biosciences focuses on partial cellular reprogramming and aging biomarkers with a stated mission to extend healthy human lifespan by a decade. In 2023 the company announced its Atlas science platform and raised approximately $180M+ in early backing, with support linked to Sam Altman. Retro runs age-reversal programs across cells, mice, and early human translation, built around public-private research pipelines. Based in San Francisco, it continues scaling its platform with decade-scale grants and partnerships.

name: Gero
short_description: Models human aging mathematically to track resilience to stress.
why_relevant: Statistical proof humans have an aging clock that supplements interventies.
history: Founded in 2018 in Singapore, Gero models human aging mathematically, analyzing longitudinal health data to track physiological resilience and an organism-level aging clock. Its work with large health datasets produced statistical evidence of aging-dynamics patterns that interventions might modulate. The company has published in leading journals and built AI simulators for drug-repurposing and anti-aging discovery in partnership with pharma and research institutes. Based in Singapore, Gero remains a small but influential longevity analytics player bridging data science and medicine.

name: causaLens
short_description: Builds causal learning into enterprise decisions, not just correlation.
why_relevant: Answers 'why' in finance and ops where counters strike probability models flat.
history: Founded in 2017 in London, causaLens develops causal AI that lets enterprises answer why — not just predict what — for financial and operational decisions. It built proprietary causal-machine-learning technology and works with major banking, energy, and consumer firms, earning a reputation for explainable decision systems. The company raised over $45M in venture funding and expanded its causal AI platform for forecasting, optimization, and risk. Based in London, causaLens continues to grow across regulated sectors needing robust, interpretable models.

name: Halo Space
short_description: Stratospheric balloon capsules carrying passengers to the edge of space.
why_relevant: Lower-risk access to near-space for tourism without rocket rides.
history: Founded in 2021 in Madrid, Halo Space develops stratospheric balloon capsules that carry passengers to the edge of space using hydrogen lift, making near-space tourism cheaper and safer than rocket rides. The company completed early development flights with reduced-scale capsules and signed agreements for launch operations in locations such as Colorado. Halo is targeting commercial passenger flights within a few years at prices around $150K, with a six-hour journey at height. It remains a leading European space-tourism contender and globe-focused operator.

name: Space Perspective
short_description: SpaceBalloon vehicles float tourists six hours at the edge of space.
why_relevant: Spaceenjoyers at 100,000 feet with a champagne lounge, near BSFD.
history: Founded in 2019 in Florida, Space Perspective develops the Spaceship Neptune, a balloon capsule carrying eight passengers for six hours at 100,000 feet, with large panoramic windows and a champagne lounge. The company built and test-flew uncrewed and crewed capsules after a series of equipment upgrades from its facilities near Cape Canaveral, achieving a successful full-scale test in 2021. It raised over $70M to commercialize stratospheric flights, refine guidance and return systems, and build its Florida launch site. Based in Merritt Island, Space Perspective targets luxurious, near-space experiences without rocket propulsion.

name: Gravitics
short_description: Industrial-grade modules for commercial space stations and orbital services.
why_relevant: Sites the infrastructure innards of post-ISS commercial stations.
history: Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Everett, Washington, Gravitics develops industrial-grade habitat modules and manufacturing infrastructure for commercial space stations and orbital services. In 2023 it won a major NASA development program for Orbital Reef and other commercial destinations, designing large volume-efficient modules, including robotic integration of scaled systems. The company raised a $10M+ Series B and secured dual-use demonstration contracts with the US Space Force. Gravitics aims to supply the core pressurizable and habitable volume of post-ISS commercial stations.
